candidate.answerReason: The three pairwise intersections form a triangle whose squared side lengths are 160/9, 160/9, and 64/9. It is isosceles, neither equilateral nor right.

methods.label: Find the vertices and compare sides
methods.explanation:
Finding the intersections identifies the enclosed polygon and lets us compare its side lengths. The two sloping lines meet where
\[
3x+2=-3x+2,
\]
so their intersection is \(U=(0,2)\). Substituting \(y=-2\) into the two sloping-line equations gives the other intersections
\[
V=\left(-\frac43,-2\right),
\qquad
W=\left(\frac43,-2\right).
\]
The three lines meet pairwise at these three distinct points, so they enclose one triangle, \(UVW\).

Using the coordinate distance formula,
\[
UV^2=UW^2=\left(\frac43\right)^2+4^2
=\frac{160}{9},
\qquad
VW^2=\left(\frac83\right)^2=\frac{64}{9}.
\]
Thus \(UV=UW\), while the base \(VW\) has a different length. The triangle is isosceles and not equilateral. It is also not right, because its two longest sides are equal, whereas a right triangle has a single longest side, its hypotenuse. Therefore the answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
